newsitem.title: FINLAND: LORD MOYNE SAYS TO BUY MINORITY IN AMER. [CORRECTED 09:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: LORD MOYNE SAYS TO BUY MINORITY IN AMER. [CORRECTED 09:00 GMT]

text.p: Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne, said in a statement late on Monday he had accepted to buy 12.5 percent of votes -- 1.2 percent of shares -- in Finnish sporting goods group Amer for 75 million markka.
He had accepted the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration's (KY) offer to sell 275,000 vote-strong but unlisted K shares at 274 markka per share, he said.
"When the deal is finalised, Lord Moyne acquires 275,000 K shares from the seller for 274 markka (corrects from 264 markka) per share...," he said.
According to Amer's bylaws, the company may redeem the shares within 30 days and the other three holders of K shares have 60 days to consider redemption them, he said.

"This acquisition shows our long-term intentions regarding the investment in Amer and it naturally also leaves the door open for future ownership arrantgements with the other owners of the company," Lord Moyne said.

Lord Moyne offered early in June to buy almost 60 percent of votes in Amer for 301 million markka from the four owners of K shares. They all initially approved the deal but all but KY later pulled out.
The price agreed with KY was "in conformity with the earlier terms discussed with the sellers," Lord Moyne said.
It was now essential to go through the various options as quickly as possible to grant Amer the stable ownership it needs for a favourable development, he added.
